text: THE SILICON What the part actually is One 28 nm die under every SKU in this deck. Configuration changes; the compute does not.   DEEPGRID SEMI · PRODUCT LINES · MANAGEMENT PROJECTIONS 05  PARAMETER SPECIFICATION WHY AN INVESTOR SHOULD CARE  Process TSMC 28 nm · single die, ~57 mm² Monolithic, not chiplet — less cost and less risk.  Compute 32,768 MACs at 600 MHz · 39.3 TOPS 64 compute cubes of 512 MACs. Derived, not rounded up.  Memory 102.4 GB/s dual-channel LPDDR5 Bandwidth, not TOPS, binds multi-camera fusion.  Transformer Hardware softmax · weight-stationary attention The operation an FPGA cannot do at frame rate.  Safety Lockstep cores plus a hardware root of trust The path to an automotive safety rating.   Throughput Eleven sensor channels fused in 8.6 ms Of a 33.3 ms frame budget — 74% left unused.   The one number that explains the portfolio A part that clears eleven channels in a quarter of its frame budget configures downward into a one-channel module, a mirror unit, a radar pod or a forklift kit without redesigning the compute. That headroom is why fifteen SKUs are one tapeout, not fifteen programmes.
notes: SoC2 specification. Headroom is what permits the SKU fan-out; every configuration below eleven channels is a firmware and front-end change, not a new die.

DEEPGRID SEMI · PRODUCT LINES · MANAGEMENT PROJECTIONS 24    7 colour cameras Road left/right, side left/right, dashcam, driver and rear.   2 thermal cameras An additional sensing modality in the two mirror towers.   2 radars Front and rear range and relative-motion inputs.   The reusable product Compute and software; the installation is one application. Architecture illustration. Targets and arithmetic peaks require workload and implementation validation.        7 RGB cameras  2 thermal cameras  2 radars  IN-CAB COMPUTE  Fused perception 11 configured inputs → one perception platform
notes:
The product story starts with the compute box, not the mirrors. The proposed configuration has eleven inputs: seven colour cameras, two thermal cameras and two radars. The colour cameras cover the left and right road views, both truck sides, a forward dashcam, the driver and the rear. Two thermal cameras add another sensing modality. Front and rear radar contribute range and velocity. These inputs converge on the in-cab processor for fused perception. For an investor, the distinction matters: the proposed semiconductor and software platform is the reusable product; the sensor installation is one application of it. The illustrated configuration is not, by itself, evidence that the entire suite has been validated together.

notes:
Each mirror tower combines a road-facing camera, a one hundred and twenty degree side camera and a thermal camera. The placement is intended to complement the truck's existing mirrors. The rear camera covers directly behind the vehicle and the rear-side areas, while radar adds distance and relative-motion information at both ends. Inside the cab, the dashcam records the road and the driver-monitoring camera watches the driver. The schematic shows how these sensing roles complement each other. Overlap explains the intended design; it does not prove zero blind spots. Occlusion, calibration, mounting tolerance and environmental testing still determine actual coverage. The proposed installation also includes six ultrasonic sensors outside the headline eleven-input count, so the production sensor bill of materials needs reconciliation.
